summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational experience that explores the equipment humanity has left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through immersive 3D environments and interactive storytelling, users can discover historic landers, rovers, scientific instruments and other mission hardware.

Visitors can explore planetary landscapes, select individual objects and uncover why they were sent, how they worked, what scientific discoveries they enabled and what condition they are in today. The experience transforms space exploration history into an engaging journey for school-age audiences, helping them understand that even equipment left behind continues to tell important stories about science, technology and human curiosity.
details:
Project Overview

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an immersive, interactive digital experience designed to tell the stories of NASA hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. Instead of presenting information through traditional articles or static timelines, the project allows users to explore planetary environments and discover equipment within its original mission context.

How It Works

The experience is organised around two environments: the Moon and Mars. Users can enter a planetary landscape, explore the terrain and discover hardware placed at historically significant locations.

Selecting an object opens an interactive exploration view with information about its design, purpose, mission, scientific contribution and current status. Users can learn whether the equipment is still scientifically useful, inactive or simply remains as a historical trace of exploration.

The initial collection focuses on recognisable examples such as the Apollo Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle and Laser Retroreflectors on the Moon, along with Mars exploration hardware such as Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity.

Intended Impact

The project aims to make space science more accessible and engaging for school-age audiences. It encourages curiosity, visual learning and exploration while helping users understand the engineering challenges behind space missions and the scientific value of equipment left on other worlds.

Creativity and Innovation

The project approaches space history as a form of digital archaeology. Rather than simply showing what NASA sent into space, it focuses on what remains after a mission ends and the stories those objects continue to tell. The combination of immersive environments, object discovery and educational storytelling creates a more memorable learning experience.

Tools and Technologies

  • Figma – UI/UX design, visual systems and interaction planning.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript – Web experience development.
  • Three.js / WebGL – Interactive 3D planetary environments and object exploration.
  • AI-assisted tools – Support for ideation, content structuring, visual concept development and code generation.
